nite_assertion: 15-minute single inhalation exposure in volunteers; significant increase in blood methemoglobin at >=15 ppm (DFGOT 2014)
primary_literature_located: PMID 42128729 (methemoglobin formation reflects systemic NO uptake); PMID 41823202 (methemoglobin and NO2 levels during inhaled NO therapy); PMID 41853735 (transient neonatal cyanosis exacerbated by inhaled NO)
reviewer_note: Human inhalation route and the methemoglobin endpoint are well supported, and the dose-dependence is established. However the accessible primary literature is overwhelmingly THERAPEUTIC inhaled nitric oxide in neonates and ARDS patients, not occupational or industrial exposure. The NITE basis is a 15 ppm volunteer study reported only through DFGOT secondary documentation, which was not retrieved. Mechanistically relevant to semiconductor process gases, but the exposure scenario differs from workplace inhalation.
remaining_work: retrieve DFGOT (2014) nitric oxide documentation and the underlying volunteer study; confirm whether any occupational exposure study exists

nite_assertion: multiple reports of occupational inhalation exposure with effects on the haemal system and haematopoietic tissue: anaemia, decreased haemoglobin and haematocrit, granulocytopenia, myelosuppression (CICAD 67, 2010)
primary_literature_located: PMID 15540629 (health effects of EGEE exposure in female workers, Ind Health 2004); PMID 26325043 (haematological changes from 2-methoxyethanol and 2-ethoxyethanol, 2015); PMID 17690522 (haematological follow-up of an intervention adding rubber-glove wearing, J Occup Health 2007); PMID 6667035 (bone marrow injury in lithographers exposed to glycol ethers AND organic solvents, 1983)
reviewer_note: Genuine human occupational haematological evidence exists in primary journals. Two qualifications are decisive for route attribution: (1) the intervention study achieved haematological improvement by adding RUBBER GLOVES, which directly implies a substantial dermal exposure contribution; (2) the bone-marrow-injury report concerns lithographers exposed to glycol ethers together with other organic solvents, so single-substance attribution is not possible. This mirrors the existing treatment of 2-methoxyethanol and 2-ethoxyethyl acetate in this study.
remaining_work: full-text review of PMID 15540629 and 26325043 for exposure measurement, control group and dermal co-exposure; do NOT promote to human inhalation core while the glove-intervention finding stands

nite_assertion: methemoglobinaemia developed in 20 of 81 workers exposed by repeated inhalation at a production factory (DFGOT vol. 3, 1992)
primary_literature_located: PubMed hits for o-toluidine + methemoglobin are dominated by prilocaine / EMLA-induced methaemoglobinaemia, in which o-toluidine is the drug METABOLITE (PMID 23530020, 16723054, 14992088, 23859109); no primary occupational inhalation cohort was retrieved
reviewer_note: The Type 1 mechanism is strongly supported in humans, but almost entirely through pharmaceutical exposure to prilocaine, which is metabolised to o-toluidine. That is systemic drug exposure, not inhalation. The occupational 20/81 observation traces to DFG MAK documentation from 1992 which is not indexed in PubMed and was not retrieved, so the occupational inhalation claim remains unverified at primary level.
remaining_work: obtain DFG MAK/DFGOT vol. 3 (1992) o-toluidine documentation and identify the underlying factory study

nite_assertion: epidemiological findings in humans; chronic inhalation exposure causes haemolytic anaemia and liver and renal dysfunction (NITE/CERI/NEDO Initial Risk Assessment Report, 2005)
primary_literature_located: PMID 4063220 (toxicity in man due to stain removers containing 1,2-dichloropropane, Br J Ind Med 1985); PMID 37549028 (acute poisoning due to INGESTION of rubber cement, 2023); PMID 23808637 and 21070183 (rat inhalation toxicity and carcinogenicity studies)
reviewer_note: The human reports concern exposure to MIXED consumer products (stain removers, rubber cement) rather than to the single substance, and the clearest acute case is oral ingestion. Clean inhalation data are animal. The NITE phrase 'chronic inhalation exposure causes haemolytic anaemia' is therefore not reproducible from the accessible primary literature as a single-substance human inhalation finding. The existing v0.18 assignment of this substance to 3_uncertain / sensitivity_only should be RETAINED.
remaining_work: full text of PMID 4063220 for product composition and route; retain as sensitivity-only reference

nite_assertion: aplastic anaemia and agranulocytosis from chronic inhalation of this substance are reported (ACGIH 7th, 2001)
endpoint_type: Type 3 (blood cell counts / marrow and haematopoietic injury)
primary_literature_located: PMID 1700687 (lindane (Kwell)-induced aplastic anaemia, Arch Intern Med 1990 - TOPICAL scabicide); PMID 7512682 (lindane exposure and aplastic anaemia, Lancet 1994); PMID 1690760 (aplastic anaemia associated with organochlorine pesticide, 1990); PMID 7512355 (lindane haematotoxicity confirmed by in vitro tests on human and rat progenitors, 1994); PMID 2454526 (DIC in fatal lindane poisoning)
reviewer_note: Human marrow toxicity is well documented and is mechanistically supported by in vitro human progenitor assays, which is unusually strong corroboration for a Type 3 assignment. The exposure route in the primary case literature is however predominantly DERMAL (Kwell/scabies treatment) or systemic poisoning, not occupational inhalation. The ACGIH 'chronic inhalation' wording is a secondary summary and the underlying inhalation study was not located.
remaining_work: ACGIH 7th edition documentation for the inhalation claim; full text of PMID 7512682 and 7512355
